messages.author: 5f8d2beda4de7d2f
messages.subject: Numerous errors, feeling lost.
parts:
Hello,

I am new to SEM techniques and experiencing enough difficulty running an analysis that I think it's time I solicited opinions.  I'm sorry if these questions are a bore.

I am attempting to analyze a dataset that consists of "genotypes" and a number of environmental and geographical variables.  I want to fit a model that fundamentally proposes that composition depend on environmental and geographical conditions (i.e., I want to measure the effect environment and geography have on composition).  The hypothesis intuitively makes sense, and when I map these data, the pattern seems obvious.

I am trying to model genotypes as a latent variable that depends on the relative contributions of 4 populations; thus these data are proportions and sum to one.  The environmental data is also a latent variable that consists of 4 PC axes that summarize regional climatic conditions.  The geographical component is also latent, and consists of the region an individual is found (binary, 0 or 1), its closest proximity to the other region, and its average proximity to all points in the other region.

Prior to analysis, I standardized all of the environment and proximity data, as well as arcsin-sqrt transformed the proportional data (force of habit).

I am calling this model with the following commands:

model1 <- '
            #Regression
            #Geno ~ Environment + Geo
           
            #Latent variables
            Geno =~ k1 + k2 + k3 + k4
            Environment =~ PCaxis1 + PCaxis2
            Geo =~ IslandMin + IslandAvg + PaleoIslands
                       
            #covariation
            IslandMin ~~ IslandAvg
'
fit1 <- sem(model1, data=AvgDataS, meanstructure=T,estimator="MLR")



I receive the following errors:
Warning messages:
1: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model1, data = AvgDataS, meanstructure = T,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model1, data = AvgDataS, meanstructure = T,  :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.
3: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model1, data = AvgDataS, meanstructure = T,  :
  lavaan WARNING: residual covariance matrix is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.ov") to investigate.

My questions:
1) Does my model seem free of obvious errors?
2) What should I do about these errors? (or, what do they mean for my analysis?)
3) What are people's thought on using proportional data and a binary indicator?


Thank you for your thoughts and help.
-Daniel

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Numerous errors, feeling lost.
parts:
> My questions:
> 1) Does my model seem free of obvious errors?

> 2) What should I do about these errors? (or, what do they mean for my
> analysis?)

They are not errors. But warnings. But they suggest hat your measurement
model does not fit the data. I would start with one latent variable at a
time, and try to figure out when the trouble begins.

> 3) What are people's thought on using proportional data and a binary
> indicator?

Treating a binary indicator as continuous (as you seem to do here) is
NOT ok! You should treat it as binary, and list it in the ordered=
argument. This may very well be the cause of your trouble.

Yves.
